Use a Tier 2 architectural change: add a jointly trained causal history-pooling module to ConvRec while preserving its convolution and attention backbone. The latest model scored 0.4788 macro HR@10 versus the baseline’s 0.505, with the largest losses in Movies_and_TV and Electronics. This motivates testing whether an explicit representation of persistent user interests can improve the current endpoint representation; the results alone do not establish the cause.

The primary component is model_design: at each sequence position, compute the padding-masked cumulative mean of the network’s learned item embeddings over the available prefix. Project this pooled representation into the backbone’s hidden space, then use a learned elementwise sigmoid gate to combine it with the contextual representation before the existing final normalization and scoring head. Pooling must remain causal during training, so no position can access later interactions. This adds a direct path for broad historical preferences while letting the network learn how much contextual information to retain.

The second component is training_evaluation: keep the current sampling, ranking loss, recency weights, optimizer, and hyperparameters unchanged to isolate this architectural hypothesis. Train from seed 42 using the existing splits and select one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10 with 200 users, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42. Update the predictor writer and checkpoint reconstruction to load the pooling projection and gate, using identical sequence preparation and scoring during validation and host inference. Retain all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, and the execution deadline; every prediction must come from exactly one trained category model, without checkpoint averaging or external scores.
